points.description: Says it is a binary tree (not just any tree).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer says only 'tree' without 'binary'.

levels.says: Says it is a tree but does not specify that it is binary.

points.description: States the ordering property: for any node, the left child is smaller than the parent and the right child is larger than the parent (left < parent < right). Accept equivalent wording, including 'left subtree'/'right subtree' wording as a correct stronger statement.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only one side of the ordering is given or the ordering is stated vaguely.

levels.says: Mentions an ordering (e.g., left smaller, right larger) but gives only one side, or states it vaguely without making clear that the parent lies between the children.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the binary-tree structure and the ordering property left < parent < right. Award part marks for only one of these ideas, or for an ordering statement that gives only one side. No marks for a generic tree definition with no ordering property.
